'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[War on drugs]]
**[[United States strikes on alleged drug traffickers during Operation Southern Spear]]
***Five people are killed while others escape after the [[United States]] conducts [[airstrike]]s on three alleged drug boats at an undisclosed location. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/czdq1ple2l4o (BBC News)]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**Russian authorities report at least 24 people are killed, including a child, and dozens of others are injured in a [[Ukraine|Ukrainian]] [[drone warfare|drone attack]] on a hotel and a restaurant in Khorly in [[Russia]]n-occupied [[Kherson Oblast]], [[Ukraine]]. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2026/01/01/ukrainian-drones-killed-24-in-occupied-kherson-resort-town-pro-kremlin-governor-says-a91596 (''The Moscow Times'')]
*[[2025 Cambodian–Thai border crisis]]
**[[Thailand]] releases 18 prisoners as part of a [[ceasefire]] agreement with [[Cambodia]]. [https://apnews.com/article/thailand-cambodia-border-ceasefire-prisoners-release-65c3f6e5af81d2c8ae5156e003cbe7d7 (AP)]
*[[Syrian conflict (2024–present)|Syrian conflict]]
**An [[Islamic State]] [[Suicide attack|suicide bomber]] blows himself up near a checkpoint in [[Aleppo]], [[Syria]], after attempting to reach an [[Eastern Orthodox Church|Orthodox church]], killing one [[Syrian Armed Forces|security force]] member and wounding two more. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/12/31/suicide-bomber-kills-at-least-one-police-officer-in-syrias-aleppo (Al Jazeera)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Saudi Vision 2030]]
**The [[Six Flags Qiddiya City]] [[amusement park]] officially opens to the public in [[Saudi Arabia]], with the [[Falcons Flight]] attraction breaking records as the world's [[List of roller coaster rankings|tallest, fastest, and longest]] [[roller coaster]]. [https://www.zawya.com/en/world/middle-east/saudi-six-flags-qiddiya-city-opens-lsbixv8z (Zawya)] [https://www.arabnews.com/node/2627848/amp (''Arab News'')]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[2025–2026 Iranian protests]]
**[[Iran]] appoints [[Abdolnaser Hemmati]] as the new [[Governor of the Central Bank of Iran|leader]] of the [[Central Bank of Iran|Central Bank]] following protests over the [[Iranian rial]]'s value depreciating and the previous governor's resignation. [https://apnews.com/article/iran-currency-inflation-central-bank-governor-protests-ccc43409cfceed3096db8cf63cc0ce53 (AP)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Serbia–United States relations]], [[United States and the Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**The [[United States]] issues a temporary license allowing [[Serbia]]'s majority-Russian-owned [[Naftna Industrija Srbije]] to resume [[oil refinery|refinery]] operations until January 23 despite [[Embargo of Russian oil during the Russo-Ukrainian war|sanctions]] linked to the [[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]. [https://www.barrons.com/news/us-grants-temporary-licence-to-russian-controlled-serbian-oil-firm-nis-serbian-minister-f2fd201d (AFP via ''Barron's'')]
*[[United States–Venezuela relations]], [[Operation Southern Spear]]
**The United States imposes [[United States government sanctions|sanctions]] on four [[Venezuela]]n companies in the [[History of the Venezuelan oil industry|oil industry]] and four [[oil tanker]]s. [https://apnews.com/article/sanctions-oil-tankers-venezuela-trump-maduro-9ffee61472d248aafdc9d9bef6195c2e (AP)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2025–2026 Iranian protests]]
**A [[Basij]] officer is killed and 13 others are injured in clashes in [[Lordegan]], [[Chaharmahal and Bakhtiari province]], Iran, during demonstrations over [[Iranian economic crisis|rising living costs]]. [https://apnews.com/article/iran-protests-economy-israel-us-nuclear-8533eacbc3c502ccc5f5339ae4384399 (AP)]
*[[2025 deployment of federal forces in the United States]]
**[[U.S. president]] [[Donald Trump]] announces the withdrawal of [[National Guard (United States)|National Guard]] troops from [[Chicago]], [[Los Angeles]], and [[Portland, Oregon|Portland]] after [[Federal judiciary of the United States|federal courts]] blocked or restricted the deployments. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20251231-trump-says-pulling-national-guard-from-three-cities-for-now (AFP via France 24)]
*[[Deportation in the second Trump administration]]
**[[U.S. federal judge]] [[Trina Thompson]] of [[United States District Court for the Northern District of California|California]] blocks the [[Second presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]] from ending [[temporary protected status]] for about 89,000 [[Immigration to the United States|migrants]] from [[Honduras]], [[Nepal]], and [[Nicaragua]], ruling that the terminations may be motivated by [[Racism in the United States|racial hostility]]. [https://www.reuters.com/legal/government/us-judge-blocks-trump-move-end-protected-status-thousands-honduras-nepal-2025-12-31/ (Reuters)]
*At least three [[informal miner]]s are killed in a shooting in [[Pataz District]], [[Department of La Libertad]], [[Peru]]. Two people are arrested. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/three-killed-7-missing-new-years-eve-attack-informal-miners-peru-2026-01-01/ (Reuters)]
